boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Marks' Mills record (April 25, 1864) in the Camden Expedition [April 1864]. The April 20 arrival of the supply train, the April 23 demonstration on Camden and the evacuation of Camden on April 26-27 are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, foraging and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Infantry brigade [US] and two divisions [CS]; the live field reads zero. Britton says the escort was a brigade of infantry, four hundred First Iowa cavalry and four guns, attacked by Fagan's expedition of four thousand picked cavalry and several batteries, and outnumbered four to one. Price says the train was guarded by a brigade, 500 cavalry and six guns, and that Fagan's division of Cabell's, Dockery's and Crawford's brigades had Shelby's brigade attached.
claims.rationale: Interested and retrospective figures that differ on the cavalry and guns; no return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Confederate victory and the live result Confederate Victory. Price calls the victory complete, with all the wagons taken; Britton says the escort was overwhelmed after nearly five hours and nearly all the infantry killed, wounded or captured; NPS says the Confederates captured most of the men and all the wagons.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Steele's evacuation of Camden is campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,793 total (US 1,500; CS 293), and the live field agrees. Price claims six guns, four colors and 1,100 prisoners taken and near 500 Union killed. Britton reports Fagan's killed and severely wounded as not over 150, Cabell's brigade alone as over 200 wounded, Drake's surgeon's count of about 250 Union killed and wounded, and an estimate of 800 to 900 dead and wounded on the field, many of them Arkansas refugees and Black civilians killed with the train.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Civilian dead are not military casualties and are not merged with them.

open_questions: Drake's report (No. 16), Steele's reports (No. 2), Fagan's, Cabell's and the Arkansas regimental reports on Marks' Mills (Nos. 51-56), Shelby's report (No. 73) and the incomplete casualty returns (No. 50) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam's, 1899) is a retrospective history described on its title page as based upon official reports and the author's observations; it gives figures from Union and Confederate reports and incomplete Confederate returns, so it is not independent of the Official Records families. Price's report dated Camden, May 1864 is one family of interested Confederate accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIV, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
